chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you enter the Sacred Mosque, enter it barefoot, with calmness, dignity, and humility.
And he said: 'Whoever enters with humility, forgiveness will be granted to him, if God wills.'
I asked: 'What is humility?' He said: 'Calmness. Do not enter it with arrogance.'

So when you reach the door of the mosque, stand and say: 'Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of God and His blessings. In the name of God, by God, and from God, and whatever God wills. And peace be upon the prophets and messengers of God, and peace be upon the Messenger of God, and peace be upon Abraham.'
And all praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds.

So when you enter the mosque, raise your hands and face the House and say: 'O God, I ask You in my standing here at the beginning of my rituals that You accept my repentance, overlook my sin, and remove my burden.'
All praise is to God who brought me to His Sacred House.
O God, I bear witness that this is Your Sacred House which You made a place of return for people and a sanctuary.
Blessed and a guidance for the worlds.

O God, indeed the servant is Your servant, the city is Your city, and the House is Your House. I have come seeking Your mercy and following Your obedience, obedient to Your command and content with Your decree.
I ask You with the request of the poor one who needs You, the one fearful of Your punishment.
O God, open for me the gates of Your mercy and employ me in Your obedience and pleasure.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes and supplications for entering the Sacred Mosque in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Transmitted via the reliable chain of al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith codifies the ritual etiquette (adab) for entering the Kaaba, linking physical demeanor—specifically humility and calmness—to spiritual forgiveness. It prescribes a specific liturgy at the door involving greetings to the Prophet and Quranic verses, followed by a comprehensive supplication that acknowledges God’s ownership of the sanctuary while petitioning for the acceptance of one's repentance and deeds.
